narrative: Your application for a 1,108 DM loan for home repairs was recently reviewed, and the model determined there is a 51% probability of this being a high-risk credit situation, leading to a denial. While you have a stable skilled job and have been employed for four to seven years, certain aspects of your financial profile currently fall outside the typical range for approved applicants. To help you understand this decision, we looked at three "what-if" scenarios that show exactly what would need to change for your application to be approved. These scenarios, known as counterfactuals, identify the minimum adjustments required to flip the model’s prediction from a denial to an approval. In every single one of these three scenarios, the most critical factor identified was the status of your checking account. Currently, your account shows a negative balance of less than 0 DM, a situation shared by only about 20% of successful applicants. The analysis shows that if you simply did not have a checking account with a negative balance, the model's prediction would flip from "bad" to "good" credit risk. Interestingly, other factors like your 12-month loan duration, your 1,108 DM request, and your homeownership were already viewed favorably and did not need to change in any of the scenarios. However, your current credit history—having no previous credits or having them all paid off—is actually quite rare among approved borrowers, as only 2.3% of successful applicants share this specific trait. Most approved applicants have a more established history of managing existing or critical credits rather than having no record at all. Additionally, your installment rate of 4% of your disposable income is notably higher than the 2.94% average seen in approved loans. Despite these secondary factors, the primary barrier remains your current account standing. To improve your chances for future approval, the most effective and direct action you can take is to resolve the negative balance in your checking account. Once your account is no longer in the red, your profile, which already includes a solid employment history and property ownership, becomes much more attractive to the model. Focusing on maintaining a neutral or positive balance will likely be enough to overcome the other minor risks the model identified.
